turns.question: What does the Act say about my right to work?
turns.retrieval_query: What does the Act say about my right to work?
turns.answer:
The Act states that a person with disability has the right to work on an equal basis with others [Act cl. 28]. This includes the right to opportunity to gain a living by work freely chosen or accepted in a labour market and work environment that is open [Act cl. 28].

The Act also specifies penalties for contravention of this right:
*   A person who contravenes subsection (1) commits an offence and is liable on conviction to nominal damages of a minimum of N250,000 payable to the affected person with disability [Act cl. 28].
*   Where a company contravenes subsection (1), the company commits an offence and is liable to nominal damages of a minimum of N500,000 payable to the affected person with disability [Act cl. 28].
*   Any principal officer of the company involved in the violation is liable to N50,000 damages payable to the affected person with disability [Act cl. 28].

turns.question: Do public buildings have to be wheelchair accessible?
turns.retrieval_query: Do public buildings have to be wheelchair accessible?
turns.answer:
Yes, public buildings do have to be wheelchair accessible.

A public building must be constructed with necessary accessibility aids such as lifts (where necessary), ramps, and other facilities to make them accessible to and usable by persons with disabilities [Act cl. 4]. A person with disability has the right to access the physical environment and buildings on an equal basis with others [Act cl. 3]. This right of access to public premises is guaranteed [Factsheet Section 3]. Public facilities, including buildings, are required to be accessible and usable by persons with disabilities [Factsheet Section 3]. There is a five-year transitory period within which all public buildings or structures must be modified and accessible to persons with disabilities, including those on wheelchairs [Factsheet Section 6]. Before erecting any public structure, its plan must be scrutinized by the relevant authority to ensure it conforms with the building code [Act cl. 7]. A government or government agency, body or individual responsible for the approval of building plans shall not approve the plan of a public building if it does not make provision for accessibility facilities in line with the building code [Act cl. 7]. This procedure ensures public structures conform with a building code that includes accessibility features for persons with disabilities, including those on wheelchairs [Factsheet Section 7,8].

turns.question: Can someone without a disability park in a reserved space?
turns.retrieval_query: Can someone without a disability park in a reserved space?
turns.answer: A person without disability who parks a vehicle in a reserved space commits an offence and is liable on conviction to a fine of N5,000 [Act cl. 12]. This rule does not apply if a person with disability is a passenger in the vehicle [Act cl. 12].
